While AngularJS is a robust front-end framework for building dynamic user interfaces, NodeJS excels at handling backend operations. Many developers use AngularJS with NodeJS to create seamless, scalable applications. If you’re exploring the technical differences between AngularJS and NodeJS, or how to use Node JS with Angular JS, this guide offers clarity. Get hands-on with modern front-end tools through our AngularJS Course at 3RI Technologies, and build a solid foundation for your full stack journey. What is Node JS? Node.js is a cross-platform runtime library and an environment for running JavaScript applications outside the browser. It is a free open source tool for creating server-side JS applications. Node.js applications are written in JavaScript. This application can run on Linux and Microsoft Windows while running Node.js. This framework offers a comprehensive library of various JavaScript modules to simplify the web development process. What is Angular JS? AngularJS is a structural framework for developing dynamic web applications. Developers can use HTML as a template language, and the HTML syntax can express the application’s components briefly but clearly. It is a fully functional JavaScript framework, whose main objective is a simplification. It supports the development of dynamic one-sided web applications and supports the Programming Framework (MVC).Node.js is a cross-platform runtime environment for applications written in JavaScript, while AnglarJS is an open-source framework for developing web applications. Node.JS is a useful tool for creating fast and scalable server network applications, while AngularJS is best suited for creating client-side web applications. Node.JS is an ideal language for the development of small projects, and AngularJS is an ideal language for creating highly interactive web applications. Node.JS is written in C, C ++, and JavaScript, while AngularJS is written entirely in JavaScript. Node.js is very useful for generating database queries because JavaScript is used to write queries to the database such as MongoDB, CouchDB. This reduces the task for the developer, as he does not have to remember the syntax differences when combining the Node.js and NoSQL databases. Almost all other frameworks implement MVC by asking to split an application into MVC components. It is a difficult task, but Angular makes it easy, because it implements MVC, dividing the application into MVC components. Node.js is an ideal option for collaborative drawing/editing applications in real-time, in which the user can see the modified document live by another user, such as Dropbox or Google Docs. Angular’s declarative approach simplifies application development in a WYSIWYG way. Instead of spending time on how the program works and what loads first, developers can define what they want and Angular JS takes care of dependencies. Node.js is useful in situations where something faster and more scalable is needed. Angular is useful when creating real-time applications, such as instant messaging or chats applications. AngularJS vs NodeJS: Core architecture AngularJS was developed by Google as a framework for the development of web applications. Unlike other JavaScript frameworks, Angular is written entirely in JavaScript. It still follows the rules of JavaScript syntax. On the other hand, NodeJS was developed as a cross-platform runtime environment based on Google’s JavaScript V8 engine. It was written in several programming languages ​​- JavaScript, C and C ++. AngularJS vs NodeJS: Web Framework Unlike NodeJS, AngularJS is a web structure. Developers can use the web infrastructure to automate common development tasks while developing a variety of applications – websites, web applications, web services, and web application frameworks. NodeJS cannot be used as a web framework by JavaScript programmers. However, you have the option to choose from a variety of structures based on NodeJS – Socket.io, Hapi.js, Meteor.js, Express.js, and Sails.js . AngularJS vs NodeJS: Installation Developers can write NodeJS applications in JavaScript. However, applications must run on different platforms in the runtime environment – Windows, Linux, and macOS. Therefore, developers must install NodeJS on their computer system when creating the development environment. However, developers do not need to install AngularJS on their computer systems. You can embed AngularJS files in the code base like other JavaScript files. AngularJS vs NodeJS: Important Features NodeJS and AngularJS support MVC architecture models. However, each of the two JavaScript-based technologies has different functions. With AngularJS, programmers can use HTML as a model language. Developers can even express different components of a Web application by developing HTML syntax. AngularJS also simplifies the development of dynamic one-sided web applications, providing functions such as data binding, scope, instructions, filters, models, routing, deep links, and dependency injection. On the other hand, NodeJS as a server-side framework provides several functions that developers need to create a network and server-side applications. Developers can take advantage of the functionality provided by NodeJS to simplify the development of one-page sites, video streaming sites, and similar I / O-intensive web applications. NodeJS also helps programmers to use asynchronous APIs and a single thread event mechanism, dramatically improving the speed of code execution. Developers can even use NodeJS for Web applications to provide bulk data without buffering. AngularJS vs NodeJS: Working with Data AngularJS not only implements the MVC architecture model in other ways, but it also supports bidirectional data binding. The bidirectional data link automatically synchronizes data between the model of a web application and the components of the view. However, AngularJS does not provide a function to write queries to the database. On the other hand, programmers can use NodeJS to generate database queries in JavaScript. This makes it easier for programmers to create database queries for non-relational databases, such as MongoDB and CouchDB, overcoming syntactic differences. AngularJS vs NodeJS: Programming Language and Paradigm Support NodeJS and AngularJS support many programming languages ​​in addition to JavaScript. NodeJS supports Ruby, CoffeeScript, and TypeScript, while AngularJS supports CoffeeScript, TypeScript and Dart. Both JavaScript-based technologies even support many common programming examples. AngularJS supports object-oriented, functional, and event-driven examples. At the same time, NodeJS supports examples of object-oriented, functional, event, relational, and sub/pub programming. The functions provided by the web framework make it easy to program interactive applications in real-time. On the other hand, developers often use NodeJS to create a fast and scalable network and server applications. The functionality of the cross-platform runtime environment still helps developers create applications that need to be designed in real-time or edited together. In general, AngularJS is a client-side infrastructure, while NodeJS is a cross-platform runtime environment. JavaScript developers can integrate NodeJS and AngularJS to simplify the development of isomorphic applications.
